tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals (visible silver film around markings) happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a fresh hobby knife blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat. For stubborn cases, replace the decal and reapply with stronger solutions like Daco Strong.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Resin Kits
tips.text: For resin kits with old, dried paint, use AK Interactive's Decal Remover first to soften and lift paint. Apply with a brush, let it sit for 15-30 minutes, then gently scrape off with a plastic scaler or wooden toothpick. For stubborn spots, use a soft bristle brush and warm water to scrub gently. Rinse with water and allow to dry completely before sanding and repainting.

tips.title: Repairing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To repair broken photo-etch parts, use a jeweler's saw to carefully cut the part along the break line. Clean both sides with alcohol, then apply a small amount of CA glue along the join using a toothpick or brush. Press the parts together tightly with tweezers, applying gentle pressure while the glue sets. Once set, file or sand the join smooth, then wash the part with soap and water to remove any residue.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog a clogged airbrush, first disassemble it according to the manufacturer's instructions. Soak the nozzle and needle in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15-30 minutes. Use a soft brush to gently scrub the nozzle and needle, then reassemble the airbrush. If the clog persists, use a pin vise or needle file to carefully clean the nozzle tip, then reassemble and test with water before painting.

tips.title: Fixing Paint Reactions/Bubbling on Models
tips.text: Paint reactions or bubbling can occur due to humid conditions or incompatible paints. To fix, sand the affected area lightly with fine grit sandpaper, then apply a coat of primer to seal it. Once dry, test-spray the problematic paint in a well-ventilated area, monitoring for reactions. If the reaction persists, try a different brand or color of paint. If bubbling occurs during painting, stop immediately, allow the paint to dry, then sand and repaint with a different paint.
